Computer systems and other digital equipment have a need for permanent or temporary data storage.
INTRODUCTIONM
They require memory circuits that store programs and data for future processing.
Memory is a term used to describe the storage of data. Some memories are small and others are very large.
Memory devices range from punch cards to integrated circuits.
Large scale integration is used in producing memory circuits that store up to 16,000 bits of data.
Let's begin the lesson on 64 BIT MEMORY CIRCUIT...........................
LESSON MENU
The 64 bit memory IC is capable of storing 64 bits of data.
DISCUSSION
As of this writing, memory IC's that can store up to 64M bytes
(536,870,912 bits!) of information have been developed. This will likely increase as time goes by....
Think of the 64 bit memory circuit as being sixteen, 4 bit registers contained in one IC.
Each register stores 4 bits of data. The 4 bits contained in each register is called a WORD.

Digital circuits are designed to operate on 4, 8 or 16 bit words. Some systems use long-words that are 32 bits in length. A word is a group of bits representing a complete piece of digital information. 10101010 = 8 bit word 1010101010101010 = 16 bit word
How many words are contained in an 8k, 4 bit word memory?
To find the number of words in a memory, divide the memory capacity by the number of bits in each word.

MEMORY CAPACITY - A Memory that contains 1k, 4 bit words has the capacity of 4k bits. A Memory that contains 1k, 8 bit words has the capacity of 8k bits.
Words are stored in memory and assigned an ADDRESS. Each word has a different address.
The address is used to store new data and to locate old data for transfer.
A moving company locates your house by knowing the address.
A memory circuit locates data by knowing the address.
A memory circuit needs several register circuits to operate properly.
The address register and memory address decoder work together in storing new data.
Transferring of the address can be serial or parallel.
When new data enters memory, the address register assigns an address.
When data leaves memory, the address register knows where to find the data.
The data register is used to hold data that is sent to or removed from memory. Transferring can be serial or parallel.
The process of transferring data into memory is called WRITE.
The process of transferring data out of memory is called READ.
The 64 bit memory circuit simply stores the data until needed.
There are two general types of memory. Read Only Memories and Random Access Memories.
ROMs are used in applications that require identical data every time a process occurs.
For example, when some test equipment is turned on, a self test is performed.
The test is always the same and the data needed to run the test is read from the memory.
RAMs are used in applications that require information or instructions to go into and out of memory.
For example, measuring current with a multimeter sends data to memory.
The memory then sends data to the display to indicate the current.
The writing to and reading from memory is called random access.
Non volatile memories retain data when power is removed....
Volatile memories allow data to be stored when power is applied.
When power is removed all data in memory is lost...........
What is the process called that loads data into memory?
The transferring of data from memory to the data register is called read.

Now, let's see how the memory address decoder selects the location of data.
In this circuit, a two bit register can address four memory locations.
With 00 in the address register, gate 1 has a high output which enables word 0.
The load input is needed for RAM. If the LOAD input is true, data will transfer from the data register to word 0.
With 01 in the address register, gate 2 has a high output which enables word 1.
If the LOAD input is true, data will transfer from the data register to word 1.
With 10 in the address register, gate 3 has a high output which enables word 2.
If the LOAD input is false, data will transfer from memory word 2 to the data register.
The data 0010 is read from memory word 2.
With 11 in the address register, gate 4 has a high output which enables word 3.
If the LOAD input is false, data will transfer from memory word 3 to the data register.
The data 0011 is read from memory word 3.
Read Only Memories (ROM) do not need a load input. Data is only READ from memory.

This experiment demonstrates the operation of a 64 bit memory circuit. You will enter data and probe the outputs of the memory to verify correct operation.-
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-126 card. The purpose of this card is to demonstrate the address, write and read operations of a 64 bit memory circuit.
The COUNTER IC is the address register. Sixteen words can be addressed by this binary counter IC. S5 clears the contents of the counter.
The REGISTER IC is the data register. It uses asynchronous parallel inputs S1 through S4. S7 clears the register.
The MEMORY IC is a 64 bit memory that contains 16 four bit words.
The SN7489N 64 Bit Memory IC is used because the outputs of the chip are inverted.
If 0110 is stored at an address, the output data from that address is 1001.
The output data LEDs are LOW activated. Therefore, a low output of the chip will illuminate the LED.
Notice the output LEDs indicate the data that was entered into the memory.
The output of the memory is not fed to the data register on this card. S6 enables loading. Let's start the experiment.
